info.title: Dekka Platform API
info.description: Control plane for Dekka. All routes live under /v1.

get.description:
Returns the CSRF token and sets the `dekka_csrf` cookie if needed. Send
the token as `X-CSRF-Token` on every mutating request.

post.description:
Emails a link to `WEB_URL/magic?token=…`. For an existing account the
link signs in; otherwise it creates the account (with `name`, if given)
when opened. The response is always 202 `{"sent": true}`, so it does not
reveal whether an account exists.
Alias of `POST /v1/auth/email`, kept for one release.

Opens a sign-in or sign-up link and sets the session cookie. A sign-up
link creates the account first (verified email, personal organization,
Free plan), and `new_account` is true. Opened in a browser other than the one
that asked for it, the link answers 409 `confirm_sign_in` with the account's
`email` in details until it is sent again with `confirm: true`.

PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions JSON for `navigator.credentials.get()`.
Without an email, `allowCredentials` is empty and the browser offers any
passkey it holds for this site.
Verifies the assertion from `navigator.credentials.get()` and sets the session cookie.
PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions JSON for `navigator.credentials.create()`.
Verifies the credential from `navigator.credentials.create()` and stores the passkey.

get.description: Both are on until the user turns them off.

patch.description: Rename an organization or change its address (the part of the dashboard URL after /app/).

get.description:
The plan, its period, any scheduled change, and current usage. An ended
period is rolled forward here as well as by the reconciler.

Open invitations, newest first. Expired ones stay listed with status
expired until they are revoked or the address is invited again.

post.description:
Emails a link to WEB_URL/invite?token=… that works once for seven days.
Only owners may invite owners (403 owner_required). Refused with 409
already_member or invitation_exists, and with 403 entitlement_exceeded
(team_members) when members plus open invitations would pass the plan.

delete.description: Revoking twice is harmless. 409 invitation_accepted once it was used.

get.description:
Public. What the invitation is for, without accepting it. 400
invalid_invitation when it expired, was revoked or was used.

post.description:
Joins the organization as the invited role. Needs a signed-in session
whose verified email is the invited address (403
invitation_email_mismatch). 400 invalid_invitation when it expired, was
revoked or was used. Someone who is already a member keeps their role.

patch.description:
Only owners can make someone an owner or change an owner's role (403
owner_required). 409 last_owner when it would leave no owner.

delete.description:
Admins and owners remove others (only owners remove owners), and any
member can remove themself to leave. 409 last_owner when it would leave
no owner. The member's API keys for this organization are revoked.

post.description:
`project_id` is only for gateway keys, whose scopes are exactly
["ai"]: their requests are logged against that project and follow its
routing policy. The key is in `key`, and only in this response.

get.description: Tokens that reach only this project, newest first, revoked ones included.

post.description:
A token for CI that reaches only this project: its resources,
deployments, environments and variables. Every org-level route and every
other project answer 404 to it. `read` acts as a viewer and `write` as a
developer, never above the creator's own role. The token is in `key`,
and only in this response.
A message from the marketing site. It opens a support request that staff answer by email.

get.description: The line an admin has set to show across the top of the dashboard, if any.

post.description:
Creates an empty environment, or forks one with `fork_from`. A fork
queues the same provisioning, deployments and connection configuration a
person would by hand, and each copy counts against the plan's limits.

patch.description:
Renames the environment and its slug. Private hostnames
(`<service>.<environment>.dekka.internal`) and DEKKA_ENVIRONMENT follow
the new name from each service's next deploy.

delete.description:
Starts deleting every resource in the environment, databases included,
and marks it `deleting`. The environment disappears once the engine has
deleted them all. The default environment cannot be deleted.

get.description: Pull request previews, newest first, closed ones included.

delete.description:
Closes the preview and deletes its environment, as closing the pull
request would. A later push to the pull request opens a new one.

patch.description:
Renames, replaces the spec, changes an application's apps.dekka.cloud
subdomain, or moves a service to another region. Spec changes apply on the
next deploy; a subdomain change re-routes a running service at once. A
schedule in the spec turns a service into a scheduled job and clearing it
turns it back, which is audited as resource.kind_changed.

get.description: Runtime logs, read from the engine.

HTTP request logs for an application, read from the engine, oldest
first after `after`. Poll with `after=next_after` for new requests.

parameters.name: status

schema.description: A code such as 404, or a class such as 5xx
schema.title: Status

parameters.description: A code such as 404, or a class such as 5xx

get.description: Metrics from the engine over `window`. `simulated` is true when the engine is the mock.

Stored variables, then the system variables Dekka sets (PORT,
DEKKA_PRIVATE_DOMAIN, DEKKA_PUBLIC_DOMAIN, DEKKA_ENVIRONMENT) with
`source: "system"`, unless a stored variable of the same name overrides one.

put.description:
Creates or updates the given variables. Others are left alone, and
connection-managed keys are read-only. References are checked and refused
with 422 unknown_reference when they do not resolve. Changes apply on the
next restart or deploy.

get.description:
The service's own variables as dotenv text. Secret, sealed and
connection-managed values are left out, each with a comment line naming it.

put.description:
Saves dotenv text. Existing variables keep their secret flag and new
ones are not secret. With `replace`, user variables missing from the text
are deleted, except sealed ones; connection-managed keys cannot be set here.

post.description:
Returns a secret value in plain text. Every reveal is audited, and a
sealed variable answers 409 variable_sealed.

get.description:
Variables shared by the environment's services. A service uses one
through a `${{shared.KEY}}` reference; they are not added to every service.

put.description: Saves dotenv text as shared variables, the same way as a service's raw editor.

get.description:
The environment's manual draft: staged changes with a summary each and
`pending_count` for the pending-changes bar. An environment with nothing
staged returns an empty draft whose id is null. A `changeset` event on
the project's SSE channel says when it changes.

Changesets of every source (manual drafts, blueprint and template
plans), newest first, optionally filtered by status.

post.description:
Stages one change in the environment's manual draft, validated as the
direct endpoint would validate it (references included) against the
environment plus what is already staged. Nothing changes until the
changeset is deployed. A staged variable's value is encrypted and never
returned.

Applies every change in one transaction through the same services as
the direct endpoints, then creates one deployment (trigger config_change)
per existing service whose settings or variables changed. New services
get their initial deployment. Returns the changeset with each change's
result and every operation queued. A blueprint or template plan whose
environment changed since it was computed is marked stale and answers 409
plan_stale; an error in any change answers that change's error, with its
id in the details, and applies nothing.

Checks a blueprint without an environment. Every problem is listed
with its path, and a valid blueprint comes back with every spec
normalised (defaults filled in, kinds derived from cron schedules).

Compares a blueprint with the environment and returns the plan as a
changeset (source blueprint) of creates, updates and, with `prune`,
deletes. Nothing changes until it is deployed with
POST /v1/changesets/{id}/deploy, which answers 409 plan_stale if the
environment changed in between. An invalid blueprint answers 422
invalid_blueprint with every error.

get.description: Templates that can be planned into an environment, featured ones first. Public.

post.description:
Plans a template into the environment as a changeset (source template)
to confirm with POST /v1/changesets/{id}/deploy. Supply the template's
inputs by key; a required one left out answers 422 missing_input. Secrets
the template generates are created now, stored as secrets and never shown
in the plan. Templates only add, so a resource name already in use answers
409 name_taken. Plan limits are checked when it is deployed.

Translates a Docker Compose file into a dekka.yaml without an
environment, with a report of what carried over (applied), what changed
shape (adjusted, such as a postgres container becoming a managed database
with a connection) and what was left out (unsupported). Nothing is created.
A file that can't be read answers 422 invalid_compose.

Reads a Compose file from a GitHub repository the organization has
connected and translates it as POST /v1/compose/translate does, with
`path` saying which file was found. Services with a build section build
from that repository and branch, with their context resolved against the
file's directory. Nothing is created. A repository the GitHub App can't
see answers 422 repo_not_found (or github_not_installed when the App isn't
installed), and a branch without the file answers 422 compose_file_missing
with the paths tried.

Translates a Docker Compose file and plans it into the environment as
a changeset (source blueprint), to confirm with
POST /v1/changesets/{id}/deploy. The file is `content`, or with `path`
it is read from `repository` as POST .../compose/read does. Services with
a build section are built from `repository`; leaving it out answers 422
repository_required. A translation that doesn't validate answers 422
invalid_blueprint.

get.description:
Says whether a web service can take `subdomain`.apps.dekka.cloud. A label
is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 3 to 40 characters, not one of
Dekka's own names, and free across every organisation. The answer is a
snapshot: creating the service with `subdomain` set is what claims it, and
a label taken in between answers 409 subdomain_taken there.

parameters.name: subdomain

schema.description: The first part of an apps.dekka.cloud address
schema.title: Subdomain

parameters.description: The first part of an apps.dekka.cloud address

post.description:
Adds a custom domain to an application. The response names the CNAME
and TXT records to create before verifying. Needs a plan with custom_domains.

Looks up the TXT record now. Success makes the domain active and starts
certificate issuance; otherwise the domain is failed with the reason, and
verifying again after fixing DNS is fine.

get.description: The service's volume, or null when it has none.

post.description: Attaches a new volume to a service and queues volume.create.

delete.description: Starts deleting the volume and its data. It disappears once the engine confirms.

get.description:
Runtime profiles, sizes and images for virtual servers. Prices are a
hypothesis in GHS, and a server is billed at the hourly price for every
hour it exists. A profile is `offered` when the engine advertises it
right now, and a size is `available` when a ready host has room for it;
when the engine cannot be reached nothing is offered or available, and
`capacity_known` says so.

post.description:
Saves a public key for new servers. Private keys are refused with 422
private_key_rejected, and the same key twice with 409 ssh_key_exists.

delete.description: Servers created with this key keep it.

post.description:
Creates a virtual_machine resource and queues vm.provision. The same
as POST /v1/projects/{project_id}/resources with kind virtual_machine.
The runtime profile is fixed from here on, and the size and image must
belong to it.

delete.description:
Starts deleting the server and its disk; `?confirm=<name>` is required.
Billing stops at the end of the hour the engine confirms the delete in.

post.description:
start needs a stopped or failed server; stop and reboot a running one.
Another vm operation in progress answers 409 operation_in_progress.

Needs a stopped server, and a size from the same runtime profile whose
disk is at least as large, because disks never shrink. The server stays
stopped afterwards.

Wipes the disk and installs the image, keeping the address, size, SSH
keys and user data. `confirm` must be the server's name.

get.description:
GPU instances Dekka plans to offer. None can be provisioned yet, so
every entry is on the waitlist and has no price until a host quotes.

The organization's waitlist and reservation requests, newest first,
without withdrawn ones.

post.description:
Join the waitlist for a GPU instance, or ask to reserve some. The
request is received, Dekka contacts the organization when capacity is
available, and then closes it. Nothing is provisioned or billed.

delete.description: Withdraw a request. It is closed and no longer listed.

post.description:
Create a private inference endpoint for an open-weights model. It is
waitlisted at once, because no GPU capacity is available yet. Outside
production the AI gateway answers `private/<name>` with a simulated
reply, so an app can be built against it now.

patch.description:
Change the model, GPU class or replica range. The name, and so the
gateway model id, stays fixed.

delete.description: Delete the endpoint. The gateway stops answering its model at once.

get.description:
A Postgres database's backups, newest first: the ones taken on request
and the ones its daily schedule takes, read from the engine. Each says
where it is kept.

post.description: Takes a manual backup now (backup.create). It is kept for 30 days.

Restores a Postgres database to `target_time`, or to its latest backup
when `target_time` is left out (backup.restore). The time must fall within
the days the database's `backups.retention_days` keeps, and `confirm`
must be the database's name. Returns the operation.
Snapshots the volume now. Volumes are backed up only on request.

Restores a completed backup over the current data (backup.restore).
`confirm` must be the database's name, or the volume's service's name;
otherwise it answers 422 confirmation_required. For a database,
`target_time` restores to that moment instead of to the backup as taken.
Returns the operation.

Stores a username and password or token for a private registry. The
password is encrypted and only its last four characters are returned.

delete.description: Refused with 409 registry_credential_in_use while a service's image source names it.
Starts disconnecting. The variables are removed once the engine confirms.

post.description:
Runs one read-only statement. Anything else is refused here with 422
(empty_query, multiple_statements or query_not_read_only) before it
reaches the engine, which also runs it in a READ ONLY transaction. Rows
are capped at 500 and the timeout at 10 seconds. Every query is audited
with its length and SHA-256, never its text or result.

get.description: A page of keys matching `pattern` (glob syntax), read with SCAN.

One row per app connected to this database, with the variable it was
given and the URL with its password masked. The full value comes from
POST /v1/resources/{app_id}/env/{env_key}/reveal, which is audited.

post.description:
Issues new credentials for every active connection to this database.
Each connection goes active, pending, active: the engine rotates
(connection.configure with rotate: true), Dekka rebinds the app's
variable and restarts it. With no active connection it answers 409
no_connections.

put.description: Replaces the layout. Positions for resources outside this environment are dropped.

get.description:
Operation, resource, connection and deployment changes as they commit.
Each event's `data` is JSON with at least `type` and `id`; a comment line
is sent every 15 seconds as a heartbeat.

post.description:
Deploys an earlier healthy deployment's image again, with the settings
it ran with and the service's current variables. Returns the new
deployment, whose trigger is `rollback`. A deployment without a recorded
image answers 409 no_image, and the one serving now 409 already_active.

Takes down the deployment that is serving by queueing application.stop.
It becomes `removed` and the service `stopped` when the engine confirms.
Any other deployment answers 409 not_active.

get.description: Build and deploy log lines after `after` (a sequence number).

Streams log lines as `event: log` (with `id: <seq>` so reconnects resume
via Last-Event-ID), sends heartbeats, and ends with `event: end` once the
deployment has finished.

post.description:
Runs a scheduled job now with its start command. A job that has not
been deployed answers 409 job_not_deployed, and one whose last run is
still going 409 run_in_progress.

get.description: Runs newest first, skipped scheduled runs included.
The run's output after `after` (a sequence number).

Deployment and job run log lines in the project, newest first, paged
with a keyset cursor.

Where to send the browser to install the GitHub App for this org. It
comes back to /v1/github/setup, which links the installation.
GitHub App installation callback (the app's Setup URL).

Second half of the installation callback: GitHub has authorised the user, so
link the installation only if that user can access it.

post.description: GitHub App webhook. Verified with X-Hub-Signature-256 and deduplicated by X-GitHub-Delivery.

Development only. Builds a signed push delivery and sends it through
the same webhook handling as GitHub's.

Development only. Builds a signed pull_request delivery and sends it
through the same webhook handling as GitHub's.

get.description:
Redirects to GitHub's authorization page (or straight back with the fake provider).
Started while signed in, it links GitHub to that account, and the state records
which session asked so the callback can't link to anyone else.

Redirects to Google's consent screen (or straight back with the fake provider).
Started while signed in, it links Google to that account only.

Google's redirect target. Failures go to `/login?error=google_<reason>`
on the web app, with reason one of denied, state, unavailable, exchange
or email_unverified.

post.description:
Beacon endpoint for `navigator.sendBeacon`. Public, without CSRF, and
rate limited per IP. The body is JSON whatever the Content-Type, because
sendBeacon with a string sends text/plain. No raw IP or user agent is
stored; see ADR 0017.

path.title: Path
path.description: The page path. Query strings and fragments are dropped.

referrer.title: Referrer
referrer.description: The referring host name, such as news.ycombinator.com

props.title: Props
props.description: Up to 20 flat properties, with strings up to 200 characters

get.description: Daily counts by event name, top paths and top referrers. Staff only.

parameters.name: start

schema.description: First day, inclusive. Defaults to 29 days before end.
schema.title: Start

parameters.description: First day, inclusive. Defaults to 29 days before end.

parameters.name: end

schema.description: Last day, inclusive (UTC). Defaults to today.
schema.title: End

parameters.description: Last day, inclusive (UTC). Defaults to today.

post.description:
Starts a hosted checkout to move to a more expensive plan. Send the
browser to `authorization_url`; Paystack returns it to the callback.
Asks the provider for the checkout's outcome and applies it. Repeating it is harmless.

get.description:
Paystack's callback_url. Verifies the transaction with Paystack, applies
it, and redirects to the dashboard with `?billing=<status>&reference=`.

post.description:
Paystack webhook. Verified with `x-paystack-signature` (HMAC-SHA512 of the
raw body under the secret key) and deduplicated on the body's hash.
Ends the paid plan when the current period ends; the org then moves to Free.
Schedules a cheaper plan to start when the current period ends.
Undoes a cancellation before the period ends.

get.description: Saved Paystack authorizations. Added by a successful checkout; the authorization code never leaves the API.

delete.description: Deactivates the authorization at Paystack and removes it here.

get.description: A plain-text invoice, standing in for a PDF.
What the current period would bill if it ended now. Nothing is stored.
Each meter for the current period: quantity, included allowance and estimated charge.
Usage records for the current period, newest first.
Usage alerts, the hard spend limit, this period's estimate and whether the limit is reached.

put.description:
Replaces the alerts and the limit. Alerts already sent this period
for amounts that are kept are not sent again.

post.description:
Posts signed deploy events to `url`. The signing secret is in
`secret`, and only in this response. Refused with 422
invalid_webhook_url for a URL that is not http(s), or in production not
https or not public.

delete.description: Deletes the webhook and its delivery history.

post.description: Replaces the signing secret at once. The new one is in `secret`, and only in this response.

Sends a `webhook.test` event now, even when the webhook is turned off,
and returns the delivery with the endpoint's answer. A failed test is not
retried.

get.description: Newest first.

post.description:
Queues a delivered or failed delivery again, with the same id and body
and a fresh set of attempts. 409 delivery_pending while it is still being sent.

get.description:
Every model in the catalogue at the providers' list prices in US
dollars, which are a snapshot to check before launch. Both providers
process requests in the United States, outside Ghana.
The org's own OpenAI and Anthropic keys, newest first, revoked ones included.

post.description:
Stores the key encrypted and replaces the provider's current key, if
any. OpenAI keys start with sk- and Anthropic keys with sk-ant-. Only the
last four characters are shown again.

get.description:
The project's routing rules. A project that never saved any allows every
available model from both providers, with no fallback and no cap.

put.description:
Replaces the rules. Every model named must be in the catalogue and come
from an allowed provider, and with allowed_models set, each fallback must
be among them. The cap is in US dollars at list price per calendar month.

get.description: The project's Veil settings for the gateway. Off until someone turns it on.

put.description:
Replaces the Veil settings. Custom policies are checked by Veil first, and
every error comes back with its path in 422 invalid_privacy_policy.

post.description:
Shows what Veil would do to sample text with the saved settings, or with
unsaved ones in `policy`. With Veil off it previews protect mode. Nothing
is stored.

get.description:
Gateway requests, newest first. `model` matches the requested or the
serving model. Prompts and replies are never stored.

Requests, tokens, spend at list price and errors per UTC day (every day
in the range, zeros included) and per model, with totals. `end` is
inclusive and the range defaults to the last 14 days.

OpenAI's model list: the available models this key's project may use,
then the organization's private inference endpoints as private/<slug>,
owned by `private`. Those are waitlisted and get a simulated reply
outside production.

post.description:
OpenAI-compatible chat completions. Set `model` to a catalogue id such as
openai/gpt-4.1-mini. With `stream: true` the reply is server-sent events
ending in `data: [DONE]`, and the last chunk before it carries usage. The
response headers X-Dekka-Provider and X-Dekka-Model say what answered.

200.description: A chat.completion object, or a text/event-stream of chat.completion.chunk

post.description:
OpenAI-compatible image generation with an image model such as
openai/gpt-image-2. Images come back as base64 in `b64_json` and are never
stored, so `response_format: url` answers 422. Usage counts the prompt's
text tokens and the image tokens the provider reports.

200.description: OpenAI's images response, with each image as b64_json

post.description:
OpenAI-compatible transcription, sent as multipart form data with a
transcription model such as openai/gpt-4o-mini-transcribe. The audio is
passed to the provider and never stored.

200.description: {text, usage} as JSON, or the text alone with response_format=text

post.description:
OpenAI-compatible text to speech with a speech model such as
openai/gpt-4o-mini-tts. The reply body is the audio itself, and the
X-Dekka-Provider and X-Dekka-Model headers say what answered.

200.description: The audio, in the requested format

post.description: Opens a request with its first message. Dekka staff are emailed straight away.
Adds to the conversation and reopens it if it was closed.

role.description: The caller's role now, which is the existing one if they were already a member

allowed_models.title: Allowed Models
allowed_models.description: Catalogue model ids the connected services may use, on top of the project's routing rules. Empty allows whatever the rules allow.

AiGatewayBindingSpec.title: AiGatewayBindingSpec
AiGatewayBindingSpec.description:
Access to the AI gateway for the services connected to it. Nothing
runs on the engine: the binding is running as soon as it exists.

AiModelKind.title: AiModelKind
AiModelKind.description: What a model does, which decides the endpoint that serves it.

id.title: Id
id.description: The id callers send as `model`, such as openai/gpt-4.1-mini.

kind.description: chat, image, transcription or speech, which decides the endpoint that serves the model.

input_modalities.title: Input Modalities
input_modalities.description: What the model takes in: text, image or audio.

output_modalities.title: Output Modalities
output_modalities.description: What the model gives back: text, image or audio.

context_window.title: Context Window
context_window.description: Tokens the model reads at once, or 0 where that doesn't apply.

pricing_unit.description: What the prices count: tokens, or characters of input text.

input_price_per_mtok.title: Input Price Per Mtok
input_price_per_mtok.description: List price in US dollars per million input units.

output_price_per_mtok.title: Output Price Per Mtok
output_price_per_mtok.description: List price in US dollars per million output units.

AiPricingUnit.title: AiPricingUnit
AiPricingUnit.description:
What the two list prices count, per million: tokens (input and output),
or characters of input text for speech models billed that way.

route.description: Null when the request was refused before a route was chosen.

veil_mode.title: Veil Mode
veil_mode.description: protected or detected when Veil scanned the request.

AiRoute.title: AiRoute
AiRoute.description:
Where a request was answered. `fake` is the simulated reply used in
development, and `private` is reserved for an organization's own endpoint.

totals.title: Totals
totals.description: Events by name over the whole range

project_id.title: Project Id
project_id.description: Set for a project token, which reaches only this project and gets 404 everywhere else.

key.title: Key
key.description: The full key. It is shown only in this response.

project_id.title: Project Id
project_id.description: Set for a project token, which reaches only this project and gets 404 everywhere else.

previews.title: Previews
previews.description: GitHub services in a default environment: open a preview environment for each pull request against the tracked branch

same_host_as_source.title: Same Host As Source
same_host_as_source.description: True: the backup is on the same pilot host as what it backs up

verified.title: Verified
verified.description: Always false until procurement verifies the host

target.description: resource for a Postgres backup, volume for a volume backup

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.description: daily takes one backup a day

retention_days.title: Retention Days
retention_days.description: Scheduled backups are deleted after this

path.title: Path
path.description: Dotted path into the blueprint, such as resources.0.spec.runtime.port

content.title: Content
content.description: The blueprint text, usually a dekka.yaml

spec.title: Spec
spec.description: The spec with every default filled in

variables.title: Variables
variables.description: Variable names; values are not echoed back

file.title: File
file.description: The audio, at most 25 MB, named with its extension

region_id.title: Region Id
region_id.description: A preferred region, or null for any

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: What the change does, in a sentence. Variable values are never included.

destructive.title: Destructive
destructive.description: True for deletes of databases, buckets and volumes' services

payload.title: Payload
payload.description: The change's settings. Variable values are encrypted and left out.

has_value.title: Has Value
has_value.description: True when an encrypted variable value is staged

result.title: Result
result.description: After deploying: what the change created or queued

id.title: Id
id.description: Null for an empty manual draft that has not been started

pending_count.title: Pending Count
pending_count.description: Changes waiting to be deployed, for the canvas's pending-changes bar

operations.title: Operations
operations.description: After deploying: every operation the deploy queued

deployment_ids.title: Deployment Ids
deployment_ids.description: After deploying: the deployments it created

ChatCompletionIn.title: ChatCompletionIn
ChatCompletionIn.description:
OpenAI's chat completions request. Other unknown fields are ignored,
but tool and function calling, which the gateway does not support yet,
answer 422 unsupported_feature rather than being dropped. The last stream
chunk always carries usage, as with include_usage.

authorization_url.title: Authorization Url
authorization_url.description: Send the browser here. With the fake provider it returns at once.

report.title: Report
report.description: What carried over, what changed shape and what was left out

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.description: Values to supply when planning, from Compose interpolation

needs_repository.title: Needs Repository

One change to stage. Which fields apply depends on target and action:

- resource create: `name`, `kind`, `spec`, optional `region_id`
- resource update: `resource_id`, and `name` and/or `spec` (a full replacement, as PATCH takes)
- resource delete: `resource_id`, and `confirm` (the name) for databases
- variable create/update: `resource_id` (or `resource_name` for a service staged in this changeset),
  `key`, `value`, `secret`, `sealed`
- variable delete: `resource_id`, `key`
- shared_variable create/update: `key`, `value`, `secret`, `sealed`; delete: `key`
- connection create: `from_resource` and `to_resource` (resource names, existing or staged); delete: `connection_id`
